nahhas-irab:18-18.t: لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَجابُوا لِرَبِّهِمُ الْحُسْنى: [الحسنى is] in the position of the nominative; the implied form may be "the reward of the best", and it is said: it is a name for Paradise. أولئك لهم سوء الحساب: the scrutiny, the rebuke, and the cancelling of good deeds by bad deeds.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: الَّذِينَ يُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ: in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from His words, Mighty and Majestic: إِنَّما يَتَذَكَّرُ أُولُوا الْأَلْبابِ.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: كَذلِكَ أَرْسَلْناكَ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative. الأمة is the community.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: وَالَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ ما أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَنْ يُوصَلَ: that is, they maintain their ties of kinship, and [ties with] those of the people of obedience whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded to be honoured and revered.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: وَيَدْرَؤُنَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ السَّيِّئَةَ: that is, they repel; when they are inclined to an evil deed, they reflect, restrain themselves, and repel it by seeking forgiveness and desisting. This is a good deed. They also forbid wrongdoing, by admonition or by harshness, and all of this is good. أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ.

nahhas-irab:23-24.t:
جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ: a badal (substitute) from عقبى. يَدْخُلُونَها وَمَنْ صَلَحَ: this is one of the difficult points of grammar, because most grammarians say: ضربته وزيد ("I struck him, and Zayd") is ugly until the latent/attached pronoun is reinforced. The grammarians discussed this, until a group of them said: قمت وزيد is good with an alif [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense of "with an alif" is unclear], because this is not like the genitive, since the genitive pronoun is never separated. Abū Isḥāq held that the better form is قمت وزيدا, meaning "together", unless the speech is lengthened, so that you say: قمت في الدار وزيد, and ضربتك أمس وزيد — and if you wish, you use the accusative. In this, regard is paid only to what is separated, which is treated like reinforcement (tawkīd). Abū Jaʿfar said: in my view — and Allah knows best — «من» may be in the position of the nominative, the implied form being: "Those, and whoever is righteous among their fathers, spouses and offspring, theirs is the final abode."
وَالْمَلائِكَةُ: mubtadaʾ (subject). يَدْخُلُونَ: in the position of the khabar (predicate), and the implied form is: [they enter] saying: سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ: this too was out of obstinacy, after they had seen the signs.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from (من). وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمْ بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ: that is, by His promise. أَلا: [a particle of] alerting. بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ: that is, their hearts.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is طُوبى لَهُمْ. الَّذِينَ may also be in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from «من», or meaning "I mean". And طُوبى may be in the position of the accusative, meaning "Allah has granted them ṭūbā".

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ الْجِبالُ: «أنّ» is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "if this occurred". The scholars have several views on this verse. One is that the apodosis is omitted, the implied form being "it would have been this Quran"; and it is said the implied form is "they would not have believed". Al-Kisāʾī said: the meaning is "We wished that there were a Quran by which the mountains were moved", and so this is without omission. Al-Farrāʾ has a good view on it. He said: the apodosis is in what precedes it, i.e. "and they disbelieve in the Most Merciful, even if there were a Quran by which the mountains were moved". بَلْ لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ جَمِيعاً: [جَمِيعاً] as a ḥāl (circumstantial). أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: there are several dialect forms in it: one says يائس, and one says ييئس on the pattern فعل يفعل, and one says يئس يئس, the imperfect having the same form as the past [Translator's note: the forms are distinguished only by vowelling, which the source does not show]. أَنْ لَوْ يَشاءُ اللَّهُ: in the position of the accusative.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: أَفَمَنْ هُوَ قائِمٌ عَلى كُلِّ نَفْسٍ بِما كَسَبَتْ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, indicated by وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكاءَ. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: the implied form is "like their partners". قُلْ سَمُّوهُمْ: that is, name them by a creation they created or a deed they did by their own power. أَمْ بِظاهِرٍ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ: it is said its meaning is: it has no reality; and it is said: or by an apparent statement mentioned in the scriptures. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read وَصُدُّوا with kasra on the ṣād, because the original is صددوا, and the vowel of the dāl was shifted onto the ṣād.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t:
لَهُمْ عَذابٌ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا:
Allah's cursing them, Mighty and Majestic, and the believers' hostility towards them.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
مَثَلُ الْجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ الْمُتَّقُونَ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) according to Sībawayh; the implied form for him is: "In what is related to you is the likeness of the Garden", or "The likeness of the Garden is in what We relate to you". Al-Farrāʾ said: what makes it nominative is تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ, the meaning being "the Garden that the God-fearing were promised, rivers flow beneath it", as one says: حلية فلان أسمر ("so-and-so's description: dark"). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: whoever says مثل means صفة (description) has erred, because one says only:
صفة فلان أنه ظريف وأنه كريم ("so-and-so's description is that he is witty and generous"), and one says: مثل زيد مثل عمرو ("Zayd's likeness is ʿAmr's likeness"). «مثل» is taken from المثال (pattern) and الحذو (model), while صفة is taken from التحلية (portraying) and النعت (describing). The implied form is only: "In what is related to you is the likeness of the Garden." أُكُلُها دائِمٌ: and in it is such-and-such, and in it is such-and-such. تِلْكَ عُقْبَى الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا: mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate), and likewise وَعُقْبَى الْكافِرِينَ النَّارُ.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: وَالَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ: it is said He means by it the believers, and the Book is the Quran. وَمِنَ الْأَحْزابِ: that is, those who banded together in enmity to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; and the believers reject what did not agree with them. It is also said: those given the Book are the Jews and the Christians, who rejoice at the Quran because it confirms their prophets and their scriptures, even if they did not believe in Muḥammad ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:38-39.t: وَما كانَ لِرَسُولٍ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ بِآيَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ: that is, except by His permitting him to ask for the sign, so that he knows there is benefit in that. لِكُلِّ أَجَلٍ كِتابٌ: that is, for every nation there is a written decree and a determined, decided matter which the angels come to know, so that Allah's power, Mighty and Majestic, is known thereby; and likewise وَعِنْدَهُ أُمُّ الْكِتابِ. We have already explained the meaning of يَمْحُوا اللَّهُ ما يَشاءُ وَيُثْبِتُ.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: وَإِنْ ما نُرِيَنَّكَ: in the position of the jussive by the condition, and the nūn entered for emphasis.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t:
نَنْقُصُها مِنْ أَطْرافِها: the plural of طرف. We have mentioned the view of the exegetes on it. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: الطرف is the noble part of everything, and its plural is أطراف, as al-Aʿshā said: [al-Ṭawīl] 244-
هم الطّرف النّاكي العدوّ وأنتم ... بقصوى ثلاث تأكلون الوقائصا ]
(They are the noble ones who wound the enemy, while you, at the farthest of three [stages], eat the broken-necked beasts.)
He said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: «Knowledge is valleys; in whichever valley you take of it, you will be exhausted, so take from everything a ṭaraf» — i.e. the choicest. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said نَنْقُصُها مِنْ أَطْرافِها, i.e. by [taking] its scholars, and the scholars are the choicest, the noble. From this is «He does not know which of his two ṭarafs is longer», i.e. he does not know, because of his simple-mindedness, whether nobility comes to him from his father's side or his mother's side. الطّرف is also the noble horse, and الطّارف is newly acquired property.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: فَلِلَّهِ الْمَكْرُ جَمِيعاً: that is, to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, belongs the abiding plotting that encompasses its people. The meaning of plotting on the part of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is that He sends down punishment upon whoever deserves it from where he does not know. وَسَيَعْلَمُ الْكُفَّارُ: and الكافر [in the other reading] has the same meaning, a singular standing for a plural.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: قُلْ كَفى بِاللَّهِ: [الله is] in the position of the nominative. شَهِيداً: as a specification (bayān). وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ: in the position of the genitive, conjoined according to the wording; it may also be in the position of the nominative according to the meaning. عِلْمُ الْكِتابِ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Raʿd
Medinan
﷽
﴿المر﴾: we have explained in Sūrat al-Baqara what has been said about this and its like. It is related that its meaning is: ”أنا اللَّهُ أرى“ ("I am Allah; I see"), and it is related: ”أنا اللَّهُ أعْلَمُ وأرى“ ("I am Allah; I know and I see"), and it is related that ”الـمـر“ are letters indicating the name of the Lord, majestic is His majesty.
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿تِلْكَ آياتُ الكِتابِ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that what was revealed before the Qur'an is "the verses of the Book". ﴿والَّذِي أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْكَ مِن رَبِّكَ الحَقُّ﴾, i.e. and the Qur'an sent down to you is the truth. It is permissible that the position of ”اَلَّذِي“ be nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); and it is permissible that it be nominative by conjunction with ”آياتُ“, in which case ”اَلْحَقُّ“ is nominative on an implied ”هُوَ“.
And it is permissible that the position of ”اَلَّذِي“ be genitive (khafḍ), conjoined to ”اَلْكِتابِ“, the meaning being: ”تِلْكَ آياتُ الكِتابِ وآياتُ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إلَيْكَ“ ("those are the verses of the Book and the verses of that which was sent down to you"); and ”اَلَّذِي أُنْزِلُ“ [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source] may be a naʿt (adjective) of ”اَلْكِتابِ“ even though the wāw has come, with ”اَلْحَقُّ“ nominative by implication [of a pronoun]. And it is permissible that ”اَلْحَقُّ“ be an adjective of ”اَلَّذِي“, the meaning being: ”تِلْكَ آياتُ الكِتابِ والَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إلَيْكَ مِن رَبِّكَ الحَقُّ“ [Translator's note: i.e. with الحقِّ in the genitive as adjective of the genitive الذي]; but I know of no one who read it that way.

zajjaj:2-2.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي رَفَعَ السَّماواتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَها﴾: when He mentioned that they do not believe, He made known the proof that necessitates affirming the Creator, Mighty and Majestic is He, and said: ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي رَفَعَ السَّماواتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ﴾. In this there is such power and such indication that nothing is clearer than it: that the sky encompasses the earth, standing clear of it, without pillars. The meaning is "without pillars, and you see it thus".
And it is permissible that ”تَرَوْنَها“ be a naʿt (adjective) of the pillars, the meaning being: "without visible pillars"; on this view, what props it up is the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. ﴿وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ والقَمَرَ كُلٌّ يَجْرِي لأجَلٍ مُسَمًّى﴾: everything that is subdued and directed, possessing nothing for itself to free it from the subjugation — that is the meaning of al-sukhra (subjection). So the sun and the moon are subjected, running their courses along which they were subjected to run.
﴿يُدَبِّرُ الأمْرَ﴾: He makes it firm. ﴿يُفَصِّلُ الآياتِ لَعَلَّكم بِلِقاءِ رَبِّكم تُوقِنُونَ﴾, i.e. He makes clear the signs that point to His power to resurrect you, so that you may be certain; for they used to deny the resurrection, so they were informed that He who created the heavens, and brought man into being when he had been nothing, is able to bring him back.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَدَّ الأرْضَ﴾: after making clear the signs of the sky, He directed them to the signs of the earth, and said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَدَّ الأرْضَ﴾. It is related in the exegesis that it was round and then was stretched out; its meaning is "He spread out the earth", and placed in it rawāsī, i.e. firm mountains. One says: ”قَدْ رَسا الشَّيْءُ، يَرْسُو، رُسُوًّا، فَهو راسٍ“ when something is firm. ﴿وَأنْهارًا ومِن كُلِّ الثَّمَراتِ جَعَلَ فِيها زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ﴾: He placed in it two kinds; and ”اَلزَّوْجُ“ is the single one that has no partner [Translator's note: so in the source]. ﴿يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهارَ﴾, and it is also read: ”يَغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهارَ“. Then He made known that in these things mentioned there is proof and clear signs, and said: ﴿إنَّ في ذَلِكَ لآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾

zajjaj:4-4.t:
Then He added to their proof, and said: ﴿وَفِي الأرْضِ قِطَعٌ مُتَجاوِراتٌ﴾. It is related in the exegesis that they adjoin one another, some of them cultivated and some not cultivated; and likewise in the exegesis its meaning is: ”قِطَعٌ مُتَجاوِراتٌ“ ("neighbouring tracts"). ﴿وَجَنّاتٌ مِن أعْنابٍ﴾: the best is the nominative ”جَنّاتٌ“, the meaning being: "and in the earth are neighbouring tracts, and between them gardens".
The accusative ”جَنّاتٍ“ is also permissible, and it is read ”وَجَنّاتٍ مِن أعْنابٍ“, the meaning being: "He placed in it firm mountains, and placed in it gardens of grapes". And it is permissible that ”وَجَنّاتٍ“ be genitive (khafḍ), co-ordinated (nasaq) with ”كُلِّ“, the meaning being: "and of every fruit He placed in it two pairs, and of gardens of grapes". ﴿وَزَرْعٌ﴾: as for ”وَزَرْعٌ“, both the nominative and the genitive are permissible in it, and likewise ﴿صِنْوانٌ وغَيْرُ صِنْوانٍ﴾. ”اَلصِّنْوانُ“ is the plural of ”صِنْوٌ“ and ”صُنْوٌ“; and the meaning of ”اَلصِّنْوانُ“ is that the root is one, and from it grow two palm trees, three, or more.
In the plural of ”صِنْوٌ“, ”أصْناءٌ“ is also permissible, like ”عِدْلٌ“ and ”أعْدالٌ“, and likewise ”صُنْوٌ“; and when they are many, it is ”اَلصُّنِيُّ“ and ”اَلصِّنِيُّ“. ﴿يُسْقى بِماءٍ واحِدٍ﴾: ”تُسْقى“, with tāʾ, is also permissible. ﴿بِماءٍ واحِدٍ ونُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَها عَلى بَعْضٍ في الأُكُلِ﴾: ”اَلْأُكُلُ“ is the fruit that is eaten.
And ”وَيُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَها عَلى بَعْضٍ“ is also permissible, because mention of Allah has preceded, so the meaning is "Allah prefers"; and likewise when one says ”وَنُفَضِّلُ“ with nūn, because the report about Allah is in the plural form, as He said: ﴿إنّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي ونُمِيتُ﴾ [Qāf: 43]. The Arabs were addressed in this way because they use the plural form for those whom they honour.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإنْ تَعْجَبْ فَعَجَبٌ قَوْلُهُمْ﴾: this is an address to the Prophet, upon him be peace. ﴿أإذا كُنّا تُرابًا أإنّا لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾, i.e. this is a place for wonder, because they denied the resurrection, while He had shown them, from the greatness of the creation of the heavens and the earth, what indicates that the resurrection is easier for [divine] power than what they had already perceived. As for the analysis of ”أئِذا كُنّا تُرابًا أئِنّا لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ“: the position of ”إذا“ is accusative. Whoever reads ”أئِذا كُنّا تُرابًا“ in the form of a question, and then reads ”أئِنّا لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ“, ”إذا“ is accusative by the sense of "we will be resurrected, and our creation will be renewed"; the meaning is: "when we are dust, shall we be resurrected?" — and ”أئِنّا لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ؟“ indicates what they intended.
And whoever reads ”أئِذا كُنّا تُرابًا إنّا لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ“ brings the interrogative alif onto the whole statement, and ”إذا“ is accusative by ”كُنّا“; but the statement is then in the sense of condition and requital (al-sharṭ wa-l-jazāʾ). It is not permissible for ”جَدِيدٍ“ to govern ”إذا“, because what comes after ”إذا“ does not govern what precedes it [Translator's note: presumably meant: what follows إنّ does not govern what precedes it; translated as written]; there is no disagreement among the grammarians that what comes after ”إنْ“ and ”إذا“ does not govern what precedes them.
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that whoever asks about this by way of denial after the clarification and the proof is a disbeliever, and said: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ وأُولَئِكَ الأغْلالُ في أعْناقِهِمْ﴾. It has come in the exegesis that ”اَلْأغْلالَ“ ("the shackles") are the deeds, on their necks on the Day of Resurrection.
And the proof of that in the Qur'an is His saying: ﴿إذِ الأغْلالُ في أعْناقِهِمْ والسَّلاسِلُ يُسْحَبُونَ﴾ [Ghāfir: 71] ﴿فِي الحَمِيمِ﴾ [Ghāfir: 72]. It has also been said that ”أُولَئِكَ الأغْلالُ في أعْناقِهِمْ“ means the shackles which are the deeds, and these too lead to the shackles being on their necks on the Day of Resurrection; for your saying to a man about an evil deed, ”هَذا غُلٌّ في عُنُقِكَ“ ("this is a shackle on your neck"), means that it clings to you and that you will be requited for it with punishment on the Day of Resurrection.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
﴿وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ الحَسَنَةِ﴾, i.e. they seek the punishment by their saying: ﴿فَأمْطِرْ عَلَيْنا حِجارَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 32]. ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِمُ المَثُلاتُ﴾: ”اَلْمُثُلاتُ“ is with ḍamma and with fatḥa on the mīm. Whoever reads ”اَلْمُثُلاتُ“, it is the plural of ”مُثْلَةٌ“; and whoever reads ”اَلْمَثُلاتُ“, it is the plural of ”مَثُلَةٌ“. In ”اَلْمَثُلاتُ“ three forms are permissible: one may say ”وَقَدْ خَلَتْ اَلْمُثْلاتُ“ with sukūn on the thāʾ; fatḥa on the thāʾ is permissible: ”اَلْمُثَلاتُ“; and whoever reads ”اَلْمُثُلاتُ“ puts ḍamma on both the thāʾ and the mīm — it is quiescent in the singular and has ḍamma in the plural, and this ḍamma is a compensation for the dropping of the feminine tāʾ; and whoever gives fatḥa does so because fatḥa is the lightest of the vowels. The transmitters related:
؎وَلَمّا رَأوْنا بادِيًا رُكُباتُنا عَلى مَوْطِنٍ لا نَخْلِطُ الجِدَّ بِالهَزْلِ
(When they saw us, our knees showing, in a place where we do not mix earnest with jest.)
And whoever reads ”اَلْمُثْلاتُ“ with sukūn on the thāʾ does so because in everything with ḍamma or kasra, such as ”رُسُلٌ“, ”عَضُدٌ“ and ”فَخِذٌ“, making it quiescent is permissible because of the heaviness of the ḍamma and kasra. The meaning is that they are hastening the punishment, while there has already preceded punishment that was an exemplary chastisement (muthla), and in which there was a deterrent lesson for them, had they taken heed.

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلا أُنْـزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِن رَبِّهِ﴾: its meaning is: "why has there not been sent down to him?" They only sought signs other than those the Prophet ﷺ brought, such as the splitting of the moon, and the Qur'an, of which they were challenged to bring a sūra like it, and things of this kind; they sought signs like those of ʿĪsā and Mūsā. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that every people has a guide, and said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إنَّما أنْتَ مُنْذِرٌ ولِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هادٍ﴾, i.e. a prophet and a caller to Allah who calls them with the signs he is given, not with what they want and dictate.

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿وَما تَغِيضُ الأرْحامُ وما تَزْدادُ﴾: the meaning of ”غاضَ“ in the language is "decreased". In the exegesis: what pregnancy falls short of nine months, and what exceeds the nine. And it has been said: what falls short of completion so that it dies, and what increases until the pregnancy is complete.

zajjaj:10-10.t:
And His saying: ﴿سَواءٌ مِنكم مَن أسَرَّ القَوْلَ ومَن جَهَرَ بِهِ﴾: the position of ”مَن“ is nominative by ”سَواءٌ“, and likewise the second ”مَن“; both are nominative by ”سَواءٌ“, because ”سَواءٌ“ requires two. You say: ”سَواءٌ زَيْدٌ وعَمْرٌو“ in the sense of ”ذَوا سَواءٍ زَيْدٌ وعَمْرٌو“ ("Zayd and ʿAmr are possessors of equality"), because ”سَواءٌ“ is a maṣdar (verbal noun), so what follows it cannot be nominative except by ellipsis. You say: ”عَدْلٌ زَيْدٌ وعَمْرٌو“, and the meaning is ”ذَوا عَدْلٍ زَيْدٌ وعَمْرٌو“, because verbal nouns are not active participles; it is nouns that put their attributes in the nominative, and when verbal nouns do so, it is by ellipsis, as al-Khansāʾ said:
؎تَرْتَعُ ما غَفَلَتْ حَتّى إذا ادَّكَرَتْ فَإنَّما هي إقْبالٌ وإدْبارُ
(She grazes as long as she forgets, until when she remembers, she is all coming and going.)
The meaning is: she is one of coming and one of going; and likewise ”زَيْدٌ إقْبالٌ وإدْبارٌ“. This — I mean ”سَواءٌ“ — is among what is used very frequently, so it has been treated like active participles. It is also permissible for it to be nominative as standing in the place of ”مُسْتَوٍ“ ("equal").
However, Sībawayh considers that ugly and does not allow ”مُسْتَوٍ زَيْدٌ وعَمْرٌو“, because in his view active participles, when indefinite, are not used as mubtadaʾ (subject), owing to their being weaker than the verb; so they are not used to begin a sentence, and he treats them like the verb. The meaning of the verse is to inform them that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, knows what is hidden from them and what is witnessed. So He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن هو مُسْتَخْفٍ بِاللَّيْلِ﴾, i.e. whoever is concealed by night — and the night conceals more than the day — ﴿وَسارِبٌ بِالنَّهارِ﴾, i.e. whoever is out in the open by day on his way (sarab). One says: ”خَلِّ لَهُ سَرَبَهُ“, i.e. his way.
So the meaning is: "the one out in the open in the roads, the one hiding in the darkness, the one who speaks aloud and the one who conceals in himself — Allah's knowledge of them all is equal". Quṭrub mentioned another interpretation: he mentioned that ”مُسْتَخْفٍ بِاللَّيْلِ“ may mean "appearing by night" — this is permissible in the language — and with this ”وَسارِبٌ بِالنَّهارِ“ would mean "concealed"; one says ”اِنْسَرَبَ الوَحْشِيُّ“ when the wild animal enters its lair. The first is clear, and it is more eloquent in describing knowledge of the unseen.

zajjaj:11-11.t:
﴿لَهُ مُعَقِّباتٌ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ ومِن خَلْفِهِ﴾, i.e. a human being has angels who succeed one another, some coming after others. ﴿يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِن أمْرِ اللَّهِ﴾: the meaning is their guarding him is by Allah's command, i.e. by what Allah the Exalted has commanded them, not that they are able to repel Allah's command, as you would say: "they guard him from Allah's command" [Translator's note: the source reads ”يَحْفَظُونَهُ عَنْ أمْرِ اللَّهِ“; the sense of «كما تقول» here is unclear and is translated as written].
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما لَهم مِن دُونِهِ مِن والٍ﴾, i.e. no one besides Allah takes charge of their affairs.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
﴿هُوَ الَّذِي يُرِيكُمُ البَرْقَ خَوْفًا وطَمَعًا﴾: fear for the traveller, because in rain there is fear for the traveller, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿إنْ كانَ بِكم أذًى مِن مَطَرٍ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 102]; and hope for the settled person, because he benefits from the rain. And it is possible — and Allah knows best — that ”خَوْفًا وطَمَعًا“ means fear for whoever fears the harm of rain, since not every land benefits from rain, such as Egypt and the like, and hope for whoever hopes to benefit from it.
﴿وَيُنْشِئُ السَّحابَ الثِّقالَ﴾, i.e. those that have become heavy with water.

zajjaj:13-13.t:
﴿وَيُسَبِّحُ الرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that it is an angel who drives the clouds. It is also possible that the sound of thunder is its glorification, because the sound of thunder is among the mightiest of things, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has said: ﴿وَإنْ مِن شَيْءٍ إلا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 44]; thunder was singled out for mention because of the greatness of its sound — and Allah knows best. ﴿وَيُرْسِلُ الصَّواعِقَ فَيُصِيبُ بِها مَن يَشاءُ وهم يُجادِلُونَ في اللَّهِ﴾: it is possible that the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial), so the meaning would be: "and He strikes with them whom He wills while he is disputing about Allah". That is because it came in the exegesis «that a man of the Jāhiliyya called ”أرْبَدُ“ (Arbad) asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying: Tell me about our Lord — is He of copper or of iron? So Allah sent a thunderbolt down upon him and it killed him».
On this basis the wāw may be the wāw of ḥāl. It is also possible that, when Allah had completed the descriptions of what points to His oneness and His power to resurrect, He said after that: ﴿وَهم يُجادِلُونَ في اللَّهِ وهو شَدِيدُ المِحالِ﴾, i.e. severe in power and in punishment. One says in the language: ”ماحَلْتُهُ مِحالًا“ when you contend in strength with him until it becomes clear to him which of you is stronger; and ”اَلْمَحْلُ“ in the language is strength. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:14-14.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَهُ دَعْوَةُ الحَقِّ والَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ لا يَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهم بِشَيْءٍ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that ”دَعْوَةُ الحَقِّ“ ("the call of truth") is "the testimony that there is no god but Allah". And it is possible — and Allah knows best — that ”دَعْوَةُ الحَقِّ“ means that whoever calls on Allah affirming His oneness has his supplication answered.
﴿والَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ لا يَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهم بِشَيْءٍ﴾: then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made clear how the idols respond, since they called on idols besides Allah, and said: ﴿إلا كَباسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إلى الماءِ﴾ — except as the one who stretches out his palms towards water is answered: he calls the water to his mouth, and the water does not respond. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that their calling on the idols is like the thirsty man's calling the water to reach his mouth, ﴿وَما هو بِبالِغِهِ﴾. Some said: ﴿إلا كَباسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إلى الماءِ لِيَبْلُغَ فاهُ﴾ is like a man at the rim of a well calling the water from the bottom of the well to reach his mouth. The two explanations are one.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَن في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ طَوْعًا وكَرْهًا﴾: it has come in the exegesis that the believer prostrates willingly and the disbeliever prostrates unwillingly. And it has come that among people are those who entered Islam willingly, and among them those who did not enter until the sword was laid over his head, i.e. so he prostrated and entered Islam at first unwillingly.
And it is possible — and Allah knows best — that ”طَوْعًا وكَرْهًا“ means that the prostration is submission to Allah: among people are those who submit and accept Allah's command in what He has made easy for them, and among them are those who accept it even though there is aversion in it for them. ﴿وَظِلالُهم بِالغُدُوِّ والآصالِ﴾, i.e. "and their shadows prostrate". It has come in the exegesis that the disbeliever prostrates to other than Allah while his shadow prostrates to Allah. It has also been said that ”وَظِلالُهُمْ“ means their persons; but this goes against the exegesis.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
And His saying: ﴿أمْ جَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكاءَ خَلَقُوا كَخَلْقِهِ فَتَشابَهَ الخَلْقُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, i.e. "is it that…?", or: has anyone other than Allah created anything, so that Allah's creation became confused for them with the creation of another?
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ خالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وهو الواحِدُ القَهّارُ﴾, i.e. say that, and make it clear by the indications of His oneness that Allah has given from the beginning of this sūra, which show that He is the Creator of everything.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He, striking a parable for the disbelievers and the believers: ﴿أنْـزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَسالَتْ أوْدِيَةٌ بِقَدَرِها﴾, i.e. according to the filling He decreed for them; and ”بِقَدَرِها“ [Translator's note: presumably بِقَدْرِها, with sukūn] is permissible, i.e. according to the measure of their filling. ﴿فاحْتَمَلَ السَّيْلُ زَبَدًا رابِيًا﴾, i.e. floating, high on top of the water. ﴿وَمِمّا يُوقِدُونَ عَلَيْهِ في النّارِ ابْتِغاءَ حِلْيَةٍ أوْ مَتاعٍ﴾, i.e. seeking goods, ﴿زَبَدٌ مِثْلُهُ﴾. That which is heated in the fire seeking ornament is gold and silver; and that which is heated seeking goods is iron, brass, copper and lead.
And ”زَبَدٌ مِثْلُهُ“ means: like the foam of the water. ﴿كَذَلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الحَقَّ والباطِلَ فَأمّا الزَّبَدُ﴾, i.e. of the foam of the water, and the foam from the dross of iron, brass, copper and lead, ﴿فَيَذْهَبُ جُفاءً﴾, i.e. that goes away and is of no benefit. ”اَلْجُفاءُ“ is what the valley casts off (jafā), i.e. throws out. ﴿وَأمّا ما يَنْفَعُ النّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ في الأرْضِ﴾: as for what benefits people — water, silver, gold, iron and the rest we have mentioned — it remains in the earth.
So the likeness of the believer, his belief and the benefit of faith is like this water that is put to use for the growth of the earth's plants and the life of everything, and like the benefit of silver, gold and the other implements mentioned, because all of them remain to be benefited from. And the likeness of the disbeliever and his disbelief is like this foam that goes away as scum, and like the dross of iron and the impurities of silver and gold which the fire brings out, which are of no benefit. The position of ”كَذَلِكَ“ is accusative.
Abū Zayd said: one says ”جَفَأْتُ الرَّجُلَ“ when I throw the man down, and ”أجْفَأتِ القِدْرُ بِزَبَدِها“ when the pot casts off its foam — so ”فَيَذْهَبُ جُفاءً“ is derived from this. The position of ”جُفاءً“ is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), and it is mamdūd (with long final -āʾ). The Basrans and the Kufans all held that words such as ”اَلْقُماشُ“, ”اَلْقُمامُ“ and ”اَلْجُفاءُ“ — these things come on the pattern ”فُعالٌ“.

zajjaj:18-18.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَجابُوا لِرَبِّهِمُ الحُسْنى﴾, i.e. for them is Paradise. It may also be: "for them is the reward of those who do good", which also comes back to Paradise, as He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَلْ جَزاءُ الإحْسانِ إلا الإحْسانُ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 60]
﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهم سُوءُ الحِسابِ﴾: ”سُوءُ الحِسابِ“ ("the evil reckoning") is that no good deed is accepted from them and no evil deed is overlooked for them, and that their disbelief has nullified their deeds, as He said: ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أضَلَّ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 1]. It has also been said that ”سُوءُ الحِسابِ“ is that his reckoning is examined exhaustively and nothing of his evil deeds is overlooked; both involve ruin. The evidence for this second view is: «”مَن نُوقِشَ الحِسابَ عُذِّبَ“» ("whoever is scrutinised in the reckoning is punished"); so ”سُوءُ الحِسابِ“ would be the scrutiny (al-munāqasha).

zajjaj:22-22.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَدْرَءُونَ بِالحَسَنَةِ السَّيِّئَةَ﴾, i.e. they repel. One says ”دَرَأْتُهُ“ when I repel it. ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهم عُقْبى الدّارِ﴾ ﴿جَنّاتُ عَدْنٍ﴾ [al-Raʿd: 23]: ”جَنّاتُ“ is a badal (substitute) for ”عُقْبى“, and ”عَدْنٍ“ means residence; one says ”عَدَنَ بِالمَكانِ“ when he resides in the place. ﴿يَدْخُلُونَها ومَن صَلَحَ مِن آبائِهِمْ وأزْواجِهِمْ وذُرِّيّاتِهِمْ﴾ [al-Raʿd: 23]: the position of ”مَن“ is nominative, conjoined to the wāw in His saying ﴿يَدْخُلُونَها﴾ [al-Raʿd: 23].
It may also be accusative, as you say: ”قَدْ دَخَلُوا وزَيْدًا“, i.e. "with Zayd". Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that lineage is of no benefit without righteous deeds, so He said: ”يَدْخُلُونَها ومَن صَلَحَ“ — of those mentioned. ﴿والمَلائِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِن كُلِّ بابٍ﴾ [al-Raʿd: 23] ﴿سَلامٌ عَلَيْكم بِما صَبَرْتُمْ﴾ [al-Raʿd: 24], i.e. "saying: peace be upon you for what you patiently endured". This is an honour from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, for the people of Paradise. The meaning is "they enter upon them from every gate saying: peace be upon you"; the "saying" is left implied here because there is an indication of it in the speech.

zajjaj:27-27.t: And His saying: ﴿وَيَهْدِي إلَيْهِ مَن أنابَ﴾ means whoever returns to the truth.

zajjaj:28-28.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ is in the position of the accusative, referred back to ”مَن“; the meaning is: "He guides to Himself those who believe". ﴿وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهم بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. when Allah is mentioned with His oneness, they believe in Him without doubting. ﴿ألا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ القُلُوبُ﴾: ”ألا“ is a particle of alerting and of beginning. The meaning of ”ألا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ القُلُوبُ“ is: the hearts which are the hearts of the believers, because the disbeliever's heart is not at rest.

zajjaj:29-29.t:
﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ طُوبى لَهم وحُسْنُ مَآبٍ﴾: the reading is with the nominative in ”وَحُسْنُ مَآبٍ“, conjoined to طُوبى, as you say: ”اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، والكَرامَةُ“. If you wish, it may be accusative: ”طُوبى لَهم وحُسْنَ مَآبٍ“, i.e. "Allah has appointed for them ṭūbā and a good return". ”طُوبى“, according to the grammarians, is ”فُعْلى“ from ”اَلطِّيبُ“ (goodness); the meaning is: "the good life is theirs".
And it has come in the exegesis from the Prophet ﷺ that «”طُوبى“ is a tree in Paradise». It has been said: ”طُوبى لَهُمْ“ means "the best (ḥusnā) is theirs"; it has been said: ”طُوبى لَهُمْ“ means "good is theirs"; it has been said: ”طُوبى لَهُمْ“ is the name of Paradise in Indian; and it has been said: ”طُوبى لَهُمْ“ means "a choice (khīra) is theirs". All of this exegesis resembles the grammarians' statement that it is ”فُعْلى“ from ”اَلطِّيبُ“.

zajjaj:31-31.t:
And His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿وَلَوْ أنَّ قُرْآنًا سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ الجِبالُ أوْ قُطِّعَتْ بِهِ الأرْضُ أوْ كُلِّمَ بِهِ المَوْتى﴾: the answer of ”لَوْ“ has been left out because there is an indication of it in the speech. The idolaters had asked the Prophet ﷺ to make room for them in Mecca and move its mountains apart, so that they could take estates and orchards in it, and to bring back to life for them some people whom they named to him. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known to them that if that were done by means of any Qur'an, it would be done by this Qur'an.
What I take to be the case — and Allah knows best, and some of the philologists have said it — is that the meaning is: "if there were a Qur'an by which the earth was moved, or the dead were spoken to, they would not believe in it". The evidence for this view is His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ أنَّنا نَـزَّلْنا إلَيْهِمُ المَلائِكَةَ وكَلَّمَهُمُ المَوْتى وحَشَرْنا عَلَيْهِمْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ قُبُلا ما كانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا إلا أنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 111]
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أفَلَمْ يَيْأسِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أنْ لَوْ يَشاءُ اللَّهُ لَهَدى النّاسَ﴾: it has been said that it is a dialect of al-Nakhaʿ: ”يَيْأسِ“ in the sense of ”يَعْلَمِ“ ("know"); and they recited:
؎أقُولُ لَهم بِالشِّعْبِ إذْ يَيْسِرُونَنِي ألَمْ تَيْأسُوا أنِّي ابْنُ فارِسِ زَهْدَمِ
(I say to them in the ravine as they cast lots over me: do you not know that I am the son of the rider of Zahdam?)
And it was read: ”أفَلَمْ يَتَبَيَّنِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا“. Some of the philologists said: "Do those who believe not know with a knowledge with which they despair of its being other than what they know?" The view according to me — and Allah knows best — is that its meaning is: "Have those who believe not despaired of the faith of those whom Allah has described as not believing?", because He said: ﴿لَوْ يَشاءُ اللَّهُ لَهَدى النّاسَ جَمِيعًا﴾. ”جَمِيعًا“ is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿وَلا يَزالُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا تُصِيبُهم بِما صَنَعُوا قارِعَةٌ﴾: it has been said: "a raiding party". The meaning of ”قارِعَةٌ“ in the language is a severe calamity that befalls with a grave matter.

zajjaj:35-35.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَثَلُ الجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ المُتَّقُونَ﴾: Sībawayh said the meaning is: "among what is related to you is the description of Paradise", or: "the description of Paradise is among what is related to you"; so in his view its nominative is as mubtadaʾ (subject). Others said: ”مَثَلُ الجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ المُتَّقُونَ“ is nominative as mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate) is ﴿تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ﴾, as you say ”صِفَةُ فُلانٍ أسْمَرُ“ ("so-and-so's description is: dark-skinned"), like your saying ”فُلانٌ أسْمَرُ“; and they said its meaning is "the description of the Paradise promised to the God-fearing". Both views are good and fine. What I hold — and Allah knows best — is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has made known to us the matters of Paradise, which we have not seen nor witnessed, by means of the matters of this world that we have witnessed and seen with our eyes. So the meaning is: "the likeness of the Paradise promised to the God-fearing is a garden beneath which rivers flow, its fruit is perpetual, and its shade".

zajjaj:39-39.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَمْحُو اللَّهُ ما يَشاءُ ويُثْبِتُ وعِنْدَهُ أُمُّ الكِتابِ﴾, i.e. "Allah erases what He wills of what the guardian angels write against the servants, and confirms". Some said: ”يَمْحُو اللَّهُ ما يَشاءُ ويُثْبِتُ“ means whoever's term has come is erased, and whoever's term has not come is confirmed. It has been said: ”يَمْحُو اللَّهُ ما يَشاءُ ويُثْبِتُ“ means "He abrogates what He wills of what He has commanded, and confirms", i.e. "and keeps what He wills of His command". ﴿وَعِنْدَهُ أُمُّ الكِتابِ﴾, i.e. "the origin of the Book". And it has been said: ”يَمْحُو اللَّهُ ما يَشاءُ ويُثْبِتُ“ means "for whomever He has decreed provision and a term, He erases of that what He wills and confirms what He wills".

zajjaj:40-40.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَإنْ ما نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ الَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ﴾: ”ما“ has been brought onto ”إنْ“ to emphasise the condition, and the nūn has come in to emphasise the verb. ﴿أوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ﴾ is conjoined to ”نُرِيَنَّكَ“, and the answer of the requital (jawāb al-jazāʾ) is: ﴿فَإنَّما عَلَيْكَ البَلاغُ وعَلَيْنا الحِسابُ﴾, i.e. upon Us is the reckoning, so that We requite every soul for what it did. The meaning is: "whether We show you part of what We promised them — the making manifest of the religion of Islam over all religion — or take you before that, nothing is upon you but conveying, whether they disbelieve in it or believe".

zajjaj:41-41.t: Then Allah made known that the evidence of what they were promised had appeared and become clear, and said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أنّا نَأْتِي الأرْضَ نَنْقُصُها مِن أطْرافِها﴾, i.e. have they not seen that We have opened up to the Muslims of the land what has become clear to them? The evidence for this view is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, in another place: ﴿أفَلا يَرَوْنَ أنّا نَأْتِي الأرْضَ نَنْقُصُها مِن أطْرافِها أفَهُمُ الغالِبُونَ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 44]. What we have described has been said in explaining this verse, and more than one view has been stated: it has been said that its reduction from its edges is the death of its people and the reduction of its fruits; and it has been said: ”نَنْقُصُها مِن أطْرافِها بِمَوْتِ العُلَماءِ“ ("We reduce it from its edges by the death of the scholars"). The first view is clear.

zajjaj:42-42.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَسَيَعْلَمُ الكُفّارُ لِمَن عُقْبى الدّارِ﴾, and it was read: ”وَسَيَعْلَمُ الكافِرُ“. The meaning of ”اَلْكُفّارُ“ and ”اَلْكافِرُ“ here is one: ”اَلْكافِرُ“ is a generic noun, as you say ”قَدْ كَثُرَتِ الدَّراهِمُ في أيْدِي النّاسِ“ and ”قَدْ كَثُرَ الدِّرْهَمُ في أيْدِي النّاسِ“ ("dirhams / the dirham have become plentiful in people's hands"). Some read: ”وَسَيَعْلَمُ الكافِرُونَ“, and some: ”وَسَيَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا“; these two readings are not permissible because they contradict the agreed-upon muṣḥaf, for reading is a followed practice (sunna).

zajjaj:43-43.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ كَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكُمْ﴾: the bāʾ together with the noun is in the position of the nominative; the meaning is: "Allah suffices as witness". ”شَهِيدًا“ is accusative as tamyīz (specification). ﴿وَمَن عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ الكِتابِ﴾: ”وَمَن“ refers back to ”اَللَّهِ“, Mighty and Majestic is He. It has been said in the exegesis that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām is meant by it, and it has been said: Ibn Yāmīn. What indicates that it refers back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is the reading of whoever read: ”وَمِن عِنْدِهِ عِلْمُ الكِتابُ“ [Translator's note: so in the source; the known variant is وَمِن عِندِهِ عِلْمُ الكِتابِ / عُلِمَ الكِتابُ], ”وَمَن عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ الكِتابِ“, because the more likely thing — and Allah knows best — is that Allah does not call on anyone other than Himself as witness over His creation. Yet that exegesis is permissible, because when the proofs are established together with the acknowledgement of those who read the scriptures revealed before the Qur'an, it is a confirmed matter.
